text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
AL-RAI
- Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali discusses with top officials in the United Arab Emirates developing ties between the two countries and latest developments in Middle East peace process.
- Cabinet agrees increases to pay packages of doctors, pharmacists and nurses.
- Jordanian hospitals say they have been told by government that the World Bank is ready to share in financing comprehensive health insurance, estimated to cost 400 million dinars ($565 million).
- Cabinet approves 100 million ($141 million) private sector Red Sea tourism project to develop Aqaba's north beach. Project could provide work for 7,400 people, 10 hotels could be built.
- Prime Ministry source says basic salary of ministry secretary-generals, advisers to prime minister and other similar jobs to be increased to 600 dinars ($850) a month.
- Union bosses withdraw resignations, issued last month in protest at new press law.
- Jordan and Israel have agreed that international flights to Eilat airport will be allowed to land at Jordan's nearby Aqaba airport.
AL-DUSTOUR

- Jordanian aviation official says Kuwait has not yet responded to Jordan's request to resume flights between the two countries. Denies that Kuwaiti Airways delegation expected in Jordan this week to discuss the issue.
- Military prosecutors deny that Ahmed Daqamsa was beaten. Trial adjourned till Wednesday.
AL-ARAB AL-YAWM
- Sources say security forces arrested 54 people in recent days who infiltrated into Jordan from a neighbouring country to carry out acts of sabotage.
- United Arab Emirates Majali's visit is a step for Arab cooperation.
AL-ASWAQ
- Cabinet approves sale of Amman Bank for Investment's assets and liabilities to Arab Bank.
- Landing fees at Aqaba airport to rise four-fold to match those of Israel's Eilat airport under agreement between the two countries to transfer some flights from Eilat to Aqaba.
JORDAN TIMES
- Senate hears details of King Hussein's, Crown Prince's talks abroad.
- Jordanian officials confirm elections will take place in 1997.
